concepts.name: Subjunctive with indefinite expressions
concepts.description: Use of the present subjunctive after indefinite expressions equivalent to whatever, whenever, wherever, whoever.

attestations.source_text: The present subjunctive is used with the indefinite expressions that are the French equivalents of whatever, whenever, wherever, and whoever.

concepts.name: Concessive expressions (avoir beau, quitte à)
concepts.description: Expressions that convey concession: avoir beau + infinitive (although, however) and quitte à + infinitive (even if it means).

attestations.source_text: The expression avoir beau + infinitive can usually be translated by although or however. The expression quitte à + infinitive can usually be translated by even if it means.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Subjunctive with indefinite expressions (whatever, whenever, wherever, whoever)
grammar_rules.summary: The present subjunctive is used after the indefinite expressions quoi que, quel que, où que, and qui que.
grammar_rules.explanation: When English 'whatever' is followed by subject + verb, use the neuter 'quoi que' + present subjunctive. When 'whatever' is followed by a noun, use 'quel que' (agreeing in gender and number) + subjunctive of être + noun. 'Où que' expresses wherever, and 'qui que' expresses whoever, both followed by the subjunctive.
grammar_rules.formation: quoi que + subject + subjunctive verb; quel/quelle/quels/quelles que + subject + subjunctive of être + noun; où que + subject + subjunctive; qui que + subject + subjunctive
agreement_rules: Quel que agrees in gender and number with the noun that follows it.
grammar_rules.word_order: Indefinite expression followed by subject + verb in subjunctive.
common_traps: Confusing quoi que (whatever + verb) with quel que (whatever + noun).

attestations.source_text: The present subjunctive is used with the indefinite expressions that are the French equivalents of whatever, whenever, wherever, and whoever.

grammar_rules.summary: The expression avoir beau + infinitive is translated as 'although' or 'however'.
grammar_rules.explanation: It expresses concession: despite doing something or being something, the result is contrary to expectation.
grammar_rules.word_order: Subject + avoir (conjugated) + beau + infinitive + rest of sentence.
common_traps: Do not translate literally; it is not 'to have beautiful'.

attestations.source_text: The expression avoir beau + infinitive can usually be translated by although or however.

grammar_rules.summary: The expression quitte à + infinitive is translated as 'even if it means'.
grammar_rules.explanation: It expresses acceptance of a possible negative consequence in order to achieve something else.
usage: To express 'even if it means (doing something)'
grammar_rules.word_order: Main clause + quitte à + infinitive (often at end of sentence).
common_traps: Do not confuse 'quitte à' with 'quitter' (to leave).

attestations.source_text: The expression quitte à + infinitive can usually be translated by even if it means.

exceptions_and_traps.title: jouer à (game) vs jouer de (instrument)
exceptions_and_traps.description: The preposition changes the meaning: 'jouer à' is used for games and sports, while 'jouer de' is used for musical instruments.
exceptions_and_traps.correct_form: jouer à + game; jouer de + instrument
exceptions_and_traps.incorrect_form: jouer de + game; jouer à + instrument

attestations.source_text: Marie et Émile jouent aux échecs. Thierry joue de la guitare.

exceptions_and_traps.title: croire à (something abstract) vs croire en (person/God)
exceptions_and_traps.description: 'Croire à' is used for believing in abstract concepts (magic, progress), while 'croire en' is used for faith in a person or God.
exceptions_and_traps.correct_form: croire à + abstract; croire en + person/God

attestations.source_text: Il ne croit pas à la magie. Crois-tu en Dieu?

exceptions_and_traps.title: finir de (finish doing) vs finir par (end up doing)
exceptions_and_traps.description: 'Finir de' means to complete an action; 'finir par' means to eventually do something after a delay or hesitation.
exceptions_and_traps.correct_form: finir de + infinitive; finir par + infinitive

attestations.source_text: J’ai fini de manger. Il a fini par lui dire la vérité.

exceptions_and_traps.title: manquer (miss) vs manquer de (lack)
exceptions_and_traps.description: Without preposition, 'manquer' means to miss (an event). With 'de', it means to lack something.

attestations.source_text: J’ai manqué le cours. Cette pièce manque d’air.

exceptions_and_traps.title: manquer à quelqu'un (to be missed by someone)
exceptions_and_traps.description: The French construction 'manquer à quelqu'un' means 'to be missed by someone'; the subject and object are reversed compared to English.
exceptions_and_traps.incorrect_form: Je te manque (if meaning 'I miss you')

attestations.source_text: Tu me manques. I miss you (i.e., you are lacking to me)
